## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the issue #10988 case now works in both launchers, and stock browser entries behave exactly as before. With `Exec=/usr/bin/env LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=iHD brave %U`:

| Launcher | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| `omarchy-launch-webapp` | `/usr/bin/env --app=URL` (fails) | `/usr/bin/env LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=iHD brave --app=URL` |
| `omarchy-launch-browser` | `/usr/bin/env URL`, focus `^env.*$` | `/usr/bin/env LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=iHD brave URL`, focus `^brave.*$` |

Stock Exec lines for Chromium, Firefox, Zen, Brave, Brave Origin, Helium and Chrome produce identical arguments, private flag and focus pattern on base and head. An env-wrapped Firefox still gets `--private-window` and an env-wrapped Edge gets `--inprivate`. In the webapp launcher, extra caller arguments after the URL keep their order. The PR's own tests fail on base and pass on head, as described.

Two problems remain in wrapped forms other than `env VAR=value`, plus a gap in the new tests.

### Other wrappers pick the wrong browser token: private windows open as normal windows, and focus can jump to an unrelated window

`bin/omarchy-launch-browser` picks the first token that is not `env`, `flatpak`, `run` or `NAME=value`. That token drives both the `--help` private-flag probe and the focus pattern. For other wrappers it lands on something that is not the browser:

| Default browser Exec line (user override) | Request | Head result |
|---|---|---|
| `prime-run firefox %u` | `--private` | probes `prime-run --help`, launches `prime-run firefox --incognito` |
| Flatpak export line copied to `~/.local/share/applications` (`flatpak run … --command=firefox --file-forwarding org.mozilla.firefox @@u %u @@`) | `--private` | probes `--file-forwarding --help`, launches `… org.mozilla.firefox @@u @@ --incognito` |
| Same Flatpak line, or `env -u VAR chromium %U` | URL | launches, then `basename` gets an option-like token (`--file-forwarding`, `-u`), prints nothing, and the focus pattern becomes `^.*$` |

Firefox 156 treats `--incognito` as an unrecognized flag and opens a normal window (`BrowserContentHandler.sys.mjs`). `omarchy-hyprland-focus-app` focuses the first client whose class matches, and `^.*$` matches any window.

**Impact:** in these configurations, the private-browser shortcut opens a non-private Firefox window with no warning, and opening a link can focus an unrelated window. On base these lines launched nothing, so no working setup regresses. The PR description names `flatpak` among the handled wrappers, though, and a quiet non-private window is a worse failure than a visible one. The Firefox and focus outcomes come from source. The launcher arguments and focus patterns come from sandboxed runs with mocked launch and focus commands.

**Suggested change:** skip option tokens (`-*`) when selecting the binary, take the `--command=` value for `flatpak run`, call `basename -- "$browser_exec"`, and skip the focus call when no plausible browser binary is found.

### Quoted Exec arguments are split into broken arguments

`read -r -a` splits on whitespace and keeps literal quotes. The Desktop Entry spec requires double quotes around arguments that contain spaces. `Exec=brave "--user-data-dir=/tmp/a b" %U` now launches as:

```text
base: brave URL
head: brave '"--user-data-dir=/tmp/a' 'b"' URL
```

**Impact:** the intended profile option is lost, and the browser receives two junk arguments. Base ignored all extra Exec arguments and opened the browser normally, so this changes behavior for user overrides with quoted arguments. No stock browser entry that was checked uses quoting. A quoted `NAME=value` inside an `env` wrapper also breaks, so the wrapped form this PR targets fails there too.

**Suggested change:** unquote Exec arguments as the spec defines (double quotes with backslash escapes, `%%` as a literal `%`) without `eval`. If that is out of scope, state that quoted Exec arguments are unsupported.

**Optional test improvement:** both new mocks log `"$*"`, which erases argument boundaries. Three mutants still pass the PR tests: a browser launcher and a webapp launcher that pass the whole Exec line as one argument, and a webapp launcher that puts `--app=URL` before the executable. `! grep -E '^--app='` in `launch-webapp-test.sh` can never match, because every logged line starts with `-- `. The `uwsm-app` mock added to `launch-browser-test.sh` is never called, because the `systemd-run` mock records instead of executing. Logging one argument per line (`printf '%s\n' "$@"`) and comparing exact lines would catch all three mutants.

**Flatpak scope note:** Flatpak browsers export desktop files under `~/.local/share/flatpak/exports/share/applications` and `/var/lib/flatpak/exports/share/applications`, and neither launcher searches there. Separately, the webapp allowlist does not match Flatpak IDs such as `com.brave.Browser.desktop`, so web apps fall back to `chromium.desktop`. Both limitations exist on base too. They mean the wrapper handling only applies to Flatpak lines copied into `~/.local/share/applications`, and a default Flatpak browser now exits silently (status 1) from `omarchy-launch-browser`. A short stderr message on those `exit 1` paths would help with the silent failures described in #10988.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of both launchers, their in-repo callers and `omarchy-hyprland-focus-app`, plus the Desktop Entry spec, uwsm, flatpak 1.18.3, Firefox 156.0.1 and Chromium sources. Sandboxed runs compared base and head across 31 synthetic Exec lines with mocked `systemd-run`, `uwsm-app`, browser and focus commands, ran the PR's tests on head and base, and ran mutation checks. No browser window, compositor or user systemd session was started. Stock Exec lines for Edge, Vivaldi and Opera were not checked.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments with targeted cross-checks, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
